newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PNB shares likely to fall further --analysts.
newsitem.headline: PNB shares likely to fall further --analysts.

text.p: Shares of Philippine National Bank are likely to be pounded further this week after investors turned bearish on the stock due to its poor nine-month earnings, analysts said.
"We'll see follow-through selling in the coming week. We're looking at 300 pesos as an initial support level for PNB," said Fitzgerald Aclan, research head at Dharmala Securities.
On Friday, PNB shares fell 87.50 pesos, or 21 percent, to 322.50 pesos.

PNB earlier reported its net income from regular operations grew a mere four percent to 993 million pesos in the first nine months. Including a one-time gain from the sale of assets, its net income was much higher, up 156 percent at 3.433 billion pesos.
After announcement, PNB cut its full-year net income forecast to 1.7 billion pesos from 2.0 billion.

PNB used to be state-owned bank and its privatisation last year was welcomed by investors who drove its stock up to a year-high of 410 pesos. But analysts said its lower-than-expected performance had taken the shine off.
"It can't turn around overnight. Expectations were really high," said Wilfred Son Keng Po, sales and research head of Angping & Associates Securities.
As a government bank, PNB suffered from red tape, inefficient operations and a bloated workforce. It was also saddled with non-performing assets.

"Fundamentally, it can go down to as low as 260 pesos," said Son Keng Po. At this price, the stock would be trading at 19 times 1996 forecast earnings, a discount to the banking sector's 20 times, he added.

At an analysts' briefing after the announcement of the results, the bank had said it was launching a major restructuring, and added that cutting costs would be a top priority. But analysts said this failed to enthuse the market because its effects would be felt only after a year.
"In 1997, it will be flat growth for them," said Julie Villena, analyst at Dharmala Securities.
PNB's senior vice-president Liwayway Gener told analysts that the bank would fundamentally change the way it conducted its business.
Stock market analysts said PNB's likely drop in the week ahead would drag the whole market down.
"PNB was a shocker and we will still see its negative aftershocks in the week ahead," said Joey Salceda, president of SBC Warburg.
The main index of the Philippine Stock Exchange fell sharply, closing on Friday at 2,962.60 points, down 137.13 points, or 4.42 percent, from the week-ago level of 3,099.73.

But some analysts were hopeful that other corporate results might boost the market. Electricity distributor Manila Electric Co and Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co are expected to announce nine-month results this week.
